fields.Name: Sales: Slipped Deals
fields.UserQuestion: Which deals had their expected close date moved, by how much, and are they still open?
fields.Description: Deals whose expected close date moved (master plan §9.3 measure 8). Deals pulled FORWARD are kept rather than filtered out, because a report that only ever shows bad news is one people learn to discount.
fields.TechnicalDescription: Grain: Deal, sourced from __mj.RecordChange. Neither Deal nor DealStageEvent holds the previous ExpectedCloseDate, so the history comes from MJ's own audit trail: Entity.TrackRecordChanges is 1 on Deals and ChangesJSON carries {"Field":{"field","oldValue","newValue"}} per changed column, read with JSON_VALUE. This means slippage needs no new column and no new stamp. It does depend on RecordChange rows surviving — a retention policy on that table would silently shorten this report's history rather than break it. Date dimension: RecordChange.ChangedAt (when the slip was recorded). NetDaysSlipped compares earliest-from to latest-to, so a deal moved twice the same way is not counted twice.

fields.Name: CompanyID
fields.Description: Selling company. Omit for every company. Deal.CompanyID is server-stamped from the pipeline, so it is always present and never needs a fallback.

fields.Name: PipelineID
fields.Description: One pipeline. Omit for all pipelines.

fields.Name: PeriodStart
fields.Description: Inclusive start of the window. Omit for no lower bound.

fields.Name: PeriodEnd
fields.Description: Inclusive end of the window. Omit for no upper bound.

fields.Name: OpenOnly
fields.Description: Pass "true" to show only deals that are still open.
